gloss: snack (to go with drinks); knob; pinch

definitions.gloss: snack to accompany alcohol; drinking snack
definitions.explanation: Small dishes or finger food eaten while drinking alcohol. Synonymous with 肴 (さかな) and おつまみ (the polite form). A central concept in Japanese drinking culture.
A small protruding part that is grasped and turned or pulled, such as a volume knob or lid handle. From the verb つまむ (to pinch, to pick up).

examples.japanese: つまみ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{注文|ちゅうもん}しよう→注文する：21390_chuumon⟧。
⟦{枝豆|えだまめ}→枝豆：21197_edamame⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦ビール→ビール：01015_biiru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧つまみ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{最高|さいこう}→最高：02637_saikou⟧だ。
examples.english: Edamame is the perfect snack to go with beer.

examples.japanese: ⟦{居酒屋|いざかや}→居酒屋：09635_izakaya⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{飲|の}み→飲む：00322_nomu⟧⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧、いろいろなつまみ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{楽|たの}しんだ→楽しむ：01203_tanoshimu⟧。
examples.english: We enjoyed various snacks while drinking at the izakaya.

examples.japanese: ⟦ラジオ→ラジオ：01541_rajio⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧つまみ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{回|まわ}す→回す：01158_mawasu⟧。

examples.english: The knob on the pot lid is hot.

examples.japanese: ⟦{音量|おんりょう}→音量：10009_onryou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧つまみ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{左|ひだり}→左：00628_hidari⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{回|まわ}して→回す：01158_mawasu⟧⟦{音|おと}→音：00743_oto⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{小|ちい}さく→小さい：00025_chiisai⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I turned the volume knob to the left to lower the sound.

notes:
USAGE:
The polite form おつまみ is commonly used by customers when ordering. In casual speech, つまみ is standard. Both ⟦{酒|さけ}→酒：02211_sake⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧つまみ and ⟦{酒|さけ}の{肴|さかな}→酒の肴：08726_sakenosakana⟧ mean "food to go with drinks," but つまみ is more casual.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- おつまみ (polite form — used when ordering)
- ⟦{酒|さけ}→酒：02211_sake⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧つまみ (snack to accompany sake/alcohol)
- つまみ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ (to serve as a drinking snack — also figurative: to become a topic of conversation)
- つまみ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{回|まわ}す→回す：01158_mawasu⟧ (to turn a knob)
- つまみ{食|ぐ}い (snacking; picking at food before it's served)
